page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-2 is an instance within the Network Optimized server family based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs and 15.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core allocation of 7.5 GB per vCPU. The hardware specification contains no local disk storage, requiring external networked persistent storage, and incorporates 0 GPUs.

The configuration provides dedicated execution threads that prevent CPU contention from neighboring virtual machines. While benchmark data is unavailable for this specific profile, the allocation of 7.5 GB of memory per core allows workloads with modest processing demands to maintain moderate dataset sizes in RAM without requiring higher vCPU tiers. Network deployments require separate configuration for external addressing, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Workloads mapped to the c4n-highmem-2 profile include network proxies, in-memory caching nodes, intermediate telemetry buffers, small relational databases, and lightweight backend services requiring higher memory-per-core allocations than standard compute configurations.
